oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-01.question: In Matthew 6:9, Jesus teaches us to pray to the Father who is in heaven, asking that his name be hallowed.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-01.learningObjective: Observe the opening of the Lord's Prayer.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-01.feedbackCorrect: The prayer opens with the Father and the holiness of his name.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Matthew 6:9: that is the exact opening of the prayer taught.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-01.hint: Look at the first words of the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-02.question: In Matthew 6:9, tap who the prayer is addressed to right at the start.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-02.learningObjective: Identify to whom the prayer is directed.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-02.feedbackCorrect: The prayer does not begin with us: it begins with the Father.

feedbackWrong.a: That is what is asked to be hallowed, after the Father.
feedbackWrong.b: That is where he is, not whom we speak to.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-02.hint: It is the first word of the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-03.question: According to Matthew 6:10, what is asked to come and to be done?
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-03.feedbackCorrect: His kingdom and will come before our own needs.

feedbackWrong.a: Revenge does not appear in any petition of the prayer.
feedbackWrong.b: The will named is God's, not ours.
feedbackWrong.c: No human leader is placed at the center here.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-03.hint: See whose kingdom and will are named.

options.a: That revenge come and human justice be done
options.b: That wealth come and our will be done
options.c: That silence come and the leaders' will be done
options.d: That the kingdom come and God's will be done

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-04.question: Build Matthew 6:9 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-04.learningObjective: Recognize the order of the prayer's opening.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-04.feedbackCorrect: Father, in heaven, name hallowed: that is the opening taught.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-04.hint: The prayer begins with a call to the Father.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-05.question: In Matthew 6:10, what do we ask to come before any need of ours?
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-05.learningObjective: Remember the priority of the prayer taught.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-05.feedbackCorrect: God's rule is asked for before daily bread.

feedbackWrong.a: Forgiveness is asked later in the prayer.
feedbackWrong.c: Bread comes in the next verse, after the kingdom.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-06.question: What does Matthew 6:10 communicate that connects to this context?
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-06.learningObjective: Link Matthew 6:10 to the priority of the kingdom.
oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-06.feedbackCorrect: His kingdom and will come before bread, forgiveness, and rescue.

feedbackWrong.b: Urgent needs come in the second half of the prayer.
feedbackWrong.c: The order is the reverse: God and the kingdom come first.

oracao-sem-or-01-pai-nosso-06.hint: See what is asked for in this verse.

options.a: Kingdom before needs
options.b: Starts by asking for urgent things
options.c: Needs before the kingdom

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-01.question: In Matthew 6:11–12, daily bread and forgiveness show dependence on God for body and soul.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-01.feedbackCorrect: Eating and being forgiven: complete dependence, every day.

feedbackWrong.false: Both petitions are daily receiving from God's hands.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-01.hint: Join the petitions of the two verses.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-02.question: In Matthew 6:10, tap the little word that compares earth and heaven in the petition for God's will.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-02.feedbackCorrect: The will done in heaven is the measure for the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: That is where it should be done, not the comparison.
feedbackWrong.b: That is the model, not the comparing word.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-02.hint: Find the short word between earth and heaven.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-03.question: How does Matthew 6:12 link the forgiveness we ask for to the forgiveness we give?
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-03.learningObjective: Understand the link between receiving and giving forgiveness.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-03.feedbackCorrect: Receiving and giving forgiveness are bound in the same sentence.

feedbackWrong.b: The prayer is for forgiven debtors, not perfect people.
feedbackWrong.c: It is not a purchase: it is a heart shaped by forgiveness received.
feedbackWrong.d: They are in the same sentence, linked, not separated.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-03.hint: See the link in the middle of the verse.

options.a: We ask as we also forgive others
options.b: God forgives only those never offended by anyone
options.c: Our forgiveness buys God's forgiveness at once
options.d: Forgiving others is a separate matter from this prayer

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-04.question: How do the petitions of Matthew 6:9–10 connect?
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-04.learningObjective: Understand the order of the first half of the prayer.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-04.feedbackCorrect: Name, kingdom, and will: God at the center, in that order.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the Father's hallowed name.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-04.hint: His will on earth closes the first part.

options.a: The Father in heaven has his name hallowed
options.b: His kingdom is asked to come
options.c: His will comes to earth as in heaven

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-05.question: In Matthew 6:11, what do we ask God to give us today?
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-05.learningObjective: Understand the daily and sufficient petition.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-05.feedbackCorrect: The basics of each day, asked today, without stockpiling.

feedbackWrong.a: The petition is simple and daily, not a banquet.
feedbackWrong.c: No drink is named in this daily petition.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-05.hint: It is the basic food of every day.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-06.question: What links Matthew 6:9 to Psalms 103:13?
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-06.learningObjective: Relate the Father of the Lord's Prayer to the Psalms.
oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-06.feedbackCorrect: The psalm already called God a Father who has compassion on his children.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts call God precisely Father.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm shows compassionate nearness, not distance.

oracao-cam-or-01-pai-nosso-06.hint: Compare the name given to God in both.

options.a: Prayer without calling God Father
options.b: God as compassionate Father
options.c: God distant from his children

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-01.question: The Lord's Prayer teaches that to pray is only to list our wants, with no place for God's kingdom.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-01.learningObjective: Interpret the priority of the kingdom in prayer.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-01.feedbackCorrect: His kingdom and will come before our own needs.

feedbackWrong.true: The first half of the prayer is all about God and the kingdom.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-01.hint: Check the order of the petitions in the prayer.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-02.question: In Matthew 6:12, tap whom we also forgive, according to the prayer.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text the forgiveness given to others.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-02.feedbackCorrect: Whoever asks forgiveness is also one who forgives those who owe them.

feedbackWrong.b: That is what we ask about ourselves, not whom we forgive.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the petition made to God, not our own act.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-02.hint: Find the people at the end of the verse.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-03.question: What reading of how we should pray does the Lord's Prayer support?
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the prayer's order supports.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-03.feedbackCorrect: Name, kingdom, and will come before bread and forgiveness.

feedbackWrong.a: The prayer is all in the plural: our Father, give us.
feedbackWrong.b: No wealth is asked for in this prayer of Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: It is not a pressure formula: it is the form of a child's heart.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-03.hint: Notice the order of the two halves of the prayer.

options.a: Pray alone, never using the word we
options.b: Ask for wealth first, then praise God
options.c: Repeat words until God is forced to answer
options.d: Begin with God and his kingdom, then our needs

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-04.question: Which sequence reveals the sense of the whole Lord's Prayer?
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-04.learningObjective: See the full architecture of Jesus' prayer.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-04.feedbackCorrect: God first, our needs next, deliverance at the end.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the holiness of God's name.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-04.hint: Deliverance is the petition that closes the prayer.

options.a: Hallowed name and God's kingdom first
options.b: Daily bread and mutual forgiveness in the middle
options.c: Deliverance from temptation and evil at the end

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-05.question: In Matthew 6:13, from what do we ask not to fall, before deliverance from evil?
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-05.learningObjective: Remember the danger named at the end of the prayer.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-05.feedbackCorrect: The prayer ends by asking for guard in the hour of testing.

feedbackWrong.a: The guard asked for is moral and spiritual, in this verse.
feedbackWrong.c: Sadness is not the name given to that danger here.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-05.hint: It is the test that can make us fall.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-06.question: What links Matthew 6:9 to Romans 8:15?
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-06.learningObjective: Link the Lord's Prayer to adoption in the Spirit.
oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-06.feedbackCorrect: By the Spirit of adoption, we cry as Jesus taught: Father.

feedbackWrong.a: It is precisely the Spirit who makes us cry out this way.
feedbackWrong.c: Romans trades the spirit of slavery for that of adoption.

oracao-pro-or-01-pai-nosso-06.hint: See the cry the Spirit produces in us.

options.a: Prayer without the Holy Spirit
options.b: Children who cry Father
options.c: Slaves afraid of God

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-01.question: In Luke 18:2, the judge in the parable feared God and respected every person.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-01.learningObjective: Observe the character of the judge in the parable.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-01.feedbackCorrect: He is described precisely as one who neither fears nor respects.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Luke 18:2: the judge is the opposite of that.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-01.hint: See how the judge is introduced.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-02.question: In Luke 18:3, tap who went to the judge to ask for justice.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-02.learningObjective: Identify the character who asks for justice.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-02.feedbackCorrect: Without power or defender, it is she who goes and insists.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the other side of her case.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the place of the story, not who went to ask.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-02.hint: Find the woman in the same city.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-03.question: According to Luke 18:3, what did the widow ask of the judge?
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-03.feedbackCorrect: Her petition is justice in a case, not favors.

feedbackWrong.a: No loan appears in her petition.
feedbackWrong.c: A job is not mentioned at any point.
feedbackWrong.d: She does not want to leave: she wants justice there.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-03.hint: Hear her words to the judge.

options.a: Borrowed money to pay debts
options.b: That he judge her case against her adversary
options.c: A job in the city judge's house

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-04.question: Build Luke 18:2–3 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-04.learningObjective: Recognize the opening of the parable.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-04.feedbackCorrect: First the judge, then the widow, then her petition.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the introduction of the judge.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-04.hint: The parable presents the people before the petition.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-05.question: In Luke 18:1, Jesus teaches to pray always and never do what?
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-05.learningObjective: Remember the stated aim of the parable.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-05.feedbackCorrect: To persist is to keep going without losing heart while waiting.

feedbackWrong.b: The word in the text names the heart, not only the action.
feedbackWrong.c: Speaking with God is precisely what we must keep doing.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-05.hint: It is losing heart in the middle of waiting.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-06.question: What does Luke 18:3 communicate that connects to this context?
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-06.learningObjective: Link the widow to the teaching on persisting.
oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-06.feedbackCorrect: She returns to the judge again: the portrait of not giving up.

feedbackWrong.a: She does the opposite: she does not stop coming back.
feedbackWrong.b: She speaks and asks; she does not stay silent before injustice.

oracao-sem-or-02-persistencia-06.hint: See what the widow does repeatedly.

options.a: Giving up at the first closed door
options.b: Silence of one who accepted everything
options.c: Insistence that does not quit

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-01.question: In Luke 18, Jesus compares God to the unjust judge to teach that God answers reluctantly.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the judge and God.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-01.feedbackCorrect: The judge is a contrast: God will do justice for his own, yes.

feedbackWrong.true: Jesus' question expects a yes about God acting.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-01.hint: See whether the judge is a model or a contrast.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-02.question: In Luke 18:5, tap the word that explains why the judge finally answered the widow.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-02.learningObjective: Recognize what moved the judge's decision.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-02.feedbackCorrect: It was not the judge's kindness: it was her constancy.

feedbackWrong.b: That is her petition, not the reason he gave in.
feedbackWrong.c: She is the person; the reason is what she kept doing.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-03.question: How does Jesus use the unjust judge in Luke 18:6–7 to speak of God?
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-03.learningObjective: Understand the contrast argument in the parable.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-03.feedbackCorrect: From the worst judge to the just Father: the argument rises, not falls.

feedbackWrong.b: God chooses and defends his own; the judge respected no one.
feedbackWrong.c: The point is God's justice, not the volume of the voice.
feedbackWrong.d: God is not the reluctant judge: he is that judge's contrast.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-03.hint: Think from lesser to greater in the argument.

options.a: If even he answers, God will do justice for his chosen
options.b: God respects people less than that judge did
options.c: Only those who shout loudest are heard in heaven by God
options.d: God also needs to be worn out before he finally listens

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-04.question: How do the events of Luke 18:4–5 connect?
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-04.learningObjective: Understand the turn in the parable.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-04.feedbackCorrect: Refusal, insistence, and decision: that is the story's turn.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the judge's initial refusal.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-04.hint: His decision is the last step.

options.a: The judge refuses to answer her for a time
options.b: The widow keeps coming and insisting on him
options.c: He decides to judge her case once and for all

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-05.question: In Luke 18:7, what does Jesus affirm that God will do for his chosen ones?
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-05.learningObjective: Understand the central promise of the parable.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-05.feedbackCorrect: God's answer to the cry is to do justice.

feedbackWrong.b: He answers the cry, not with final silence.
feedbackWrong.c: Waiting is our side; his is to act with justice.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-05.hint: It is the same word as the widow's petition.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-06.question: What links Luke 18:3 to Luke 11:9?
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-06.learningObjective: Relate the parable to the teaching of Luke 11.
oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-06.feedbackCorrect: The widow lives ask, seek, and knock without giving up.

feedbackWrong.b: She asked many times, and Jesus says to keep going.
feedbackWrong.c: Her perseverance points to praying to God.

oracao-cam-or-02-persistencia-06.hint: See the three verbs of Jesus' teaching.

options.a: Ask, seek, and knock
options.b: Ask once and fall silent
options.c: Knock only on human doors

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-01.question: Luke 18 teaches us to persist trusting that God, unlike the judge, will do justice for those who cry day and night.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-01.learningObjective: Interpret persistence as an expression of faith.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-01.feedbackCorrect: Persistence with trust: it is faith, not a pressure technique.

feedbackWrong.false: Jesus' final question is whether there will be faith, not force.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-01.hint: Join the cry with the question about faith.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-02.question: In Luke 18:7, tap for whom God will do justice, according to Jesus.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text whom God defends.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-02.feedbackCorrect: It is not any pressure: it is his people crying out to him.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the one who does justice, not who receives it.
feedbackWrong.c: That is when they cry, not who receives justice.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-02.hint: Find the group after justice for.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-03.question: What reading of persisting in prayer does Luke 18:8 support?
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus closes speaking of faith: to persist is to keep believing.

feedbackWrong.a: He promises justice quickly to those who cry out.
feedbackWrong.c: The opening teaching is to pray always, without stopping.
feedbackWrong.d: God is not the tired judge: he is the just one who defends.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-03.hint: See Jesus' last question in the parable.

options.a: It proves God delays because he does not care
options.b: It is faith that keeps crying to the just God
options.c: It is unnecessary after the first prayer made
options.d: It is a way to wear God out until he gives in to us

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-04.question: Which sequence reveals the sense of Luke 18:3–8?
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-04.learningObjective: See the arc of the parable through to faith.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-04.feedbackCorrect: Insistence, God's justice, and the question about faith.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the widow before the judge.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-04.hint: The question about faith closes the parable.

options.a: The widow insists before the unjust judge
options.b: God will do justice for his own who cry out
options.c: The Son of Man looks for faith on the earth

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-05.question: In Luke 18:8, what does the Son of Man expect to find on the earth when he comes?
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-05.learningObjective: Remember what Jesus looks for: persevering faith.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-05.feedbackCorrect: The persistence he looks for has a name: faith that does not quit.

feedbackWrong.a: Human recognition is not what he looks for.
feedbackWrong.b: The widow had no force: she had believing perseverance.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-05.hint: It is the final word of Jesus' question.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-06.question: What links Luke 18:7 to Psalms 88:1?
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-06.learningObjective: Link the parable's cry to that of the Psalms.
oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-06.feedbackCorrect: The psalmist also cries day and night, without stopping.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts cry out; they do not stay silent in pain.
feedbackWrong.c: Justice is asked of God, not taken by force.

oracao-pro-or-02-persistencia-06.hint: Compare the times of the cry in both texts.

options.a: Silence accepted without crying out
options.b: Cry day and night
options.c: Justice done by one's own hands

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-01.question: In Romans 8:26, the Spirit helps us in our weaknesses when we pray.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-01.learningObjective: Observe the Spirit's help in Romans 8:26.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: His help arrives precisely where we are weak.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Romans 8:26: the help is stated.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-01.hint: See the beginning of the verse.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:26, tap who intercedes for us with inexpressible groans.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: It is he himself who takes up our cause in prayer.

feedbackWrong.a: That is where we need help, not who helps.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the manner of intercession, not who intercedes.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-02.hint: Find the subject of the second half of the verse.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-03.question: According to Romans 8:27, who knows the Spirit's purpose when he intercedes?
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-03.learningObjective: Observe who knows the Spirit's intercession.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: God, who searches hearts, understands his intercession.

feedbackWrong.a: The text affirms that God knows that purpose.
feedbackWrong.c: The groans are inexpressible: they do not depend on hearing.
feedbackWrong.d: No human group is named as interpreter here.

options.a: No one, not even God the Father himself
options.b: The one who searches the hearts of people
options.c: Only those who hear groans out loud
options.d: Only the leaders of the church in Rome

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-04.question: Build Romans 8:26–27 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: Help in weakness, groans, and intercession according to God.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the help in our weaknesses.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-04.hint: God's will closes the two verses.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:27, what does the one who searches know about our inner life?
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-05.learningObjective: Remember what God searches in Romans 8:27.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: Nothing in us is secret to the one who searches within.

feedbackWrong.b: That is what God knows of the Spirit, not of us.
feedbackWrong.c: That is for whom he intercedes, not what God searches.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-05.hint: It is our inner life, at the start of the verse.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-06.question: What does Romans 8:27 communicate that connects to this context?
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-06.learningObjective: Link Romans 8:27 to intercession according to God.
oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: He intercedes for the saints God's way, not ours.

feedbackWrong.a: He searches hearts: he knows everything in us.
feedbackWrong.c: Precisely those who do not know how to pray are helped here.

oracao-sem-or-03-espirito-06.hint: See the measure of intercession at the end.

options.a: God without knowing our inner life
options.b: Intercession according to his will
options.c: Prayer only from those who know how to speak

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-01.question: In Romans 8:26–27, the Spirit only helps those who already know how to pray very well and without weakness.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-01.learningObjective: Understand that the help is for weakness.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the opposite: the help is for the weak who do not know how to pray.

feedbackWrong.true: Not knowing how to pray as we ought is the text's starting point.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-01.hint: See for whom the help is promised.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:26, tap what we do not know how to do as we ought.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-02.learningObjective: Recognize our stated limit in prayer.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: The confession is honest: we do not even know how to pray rightly.

feedbackWrong.a: That is how he intercedes, not our inability.
feedbackWrong.c: That is where we are helped, not what we do not know how to do.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-03.question: How does Romans 8:27 complete what 8:26 says about the Spirit's groans?
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-03.learningObjective: Relate inexpressible groans and God's knowing.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: Inexpressible to us, perfectly clear to God.

feedbackWrong.b: Wordless groans are precisely what he understands.
feedbackWrong.c: It is according to God's will, the text says.
feedbackWrong.d: The one who knows is God searching hearts, not a translator.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-03.hint: See who understands what has no words.

options.a: God knows his purpose, even without words
options.b: God only understands well-formed, long prayers
options.c: His purpose is contrary to God's will
options.d: The groans need a human translator present

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-04.question: How does the argument of Romans 8:27 connect?
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: Search, know, and intercede according to his will.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the one who searches the hearts.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-04.hint: God's will is the close of the verse.

options.a: God searches the hearts of his own
options.b: He knows the Spirit's purpose
options.c: The Spirit intercedes according to his will

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:26, in what area does the Spirit help us when we go to pray?
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-05.learningObjective: Understand where the Spirit's help acts.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: His help aims exactly at our weak point.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of help in weakness, not in victories.
feedbackWrong.b: It is not eloquence he supplies: it is weakness.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-05.hint: It is our weak point, right at the start.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-06.question: What links Romans 8:26 to John 14:16?
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-06.learningObjective: Relate the Spirit's help to Jesus' promise.
oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus promised another Helper to be with us always.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts put him right at the center of the help.
feedbackWrong.b: He stays forever; he abandons no one.

oracao-cam-or-03-espirito-06.hint: See how long the Helper stays.

options.a: Prayer without the Spirit's presence
options.b: Help that abandons in weakness
options.c: Helper who stays with the disciples

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-01.question: Romans 8:26–27 teaches that our weakness in prayer does not push us away from God, for the Spirit intercedes for us.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-01.learningObjective: Interpret weakness as the place of intercession.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: Without the right words, we have a perfect intercessor.

feedbackWrong.false: Weakness is precisely where the intercession happens.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-01.hint: See what happens when we do not know how to pray.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:27, tap according to what the Spirit intercedes for the saints.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text the measure of intercession.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: His intercession is perfect because it follows the Father's will.

feedbackWrong.b: That is for whom he intercedes, not according to what.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what God knows of him, not the final measure.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-02.hint: Find the measure at the end of the verse.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-03.question: What reading of praying in weakness do Romans 8:26–27 support?
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: Our lack of words meets his intercession.

feedbackWrong.a: The text comforts precisely those who cannot formulate.
feedbackWrong.c: The one who groans is the Spirit in us, not a technique of ours.
feedbackWrong.d: Helping in weakness assumes we keep praying while weak.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-03.hint: Join our inability with his action.

options.a: God only hears those who always form perfect prayers
options.b: Even without words, we are heard and helped in him
options.c: We should produce audible groans as the right technique
options.d: We can stop praying, for he does everything alone

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-04.question: Which sequence reveals the sense of Romans 8:26?
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-04.learningObjective: See the path from weakness to perfect intercession.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: From our lack of words to the intercession God understands.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with our inability to pray.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-04.hint: The groans understood by God close the path.

options.a: We do not know how to pray as we ought
options.b: The Spirit himself takes up our intercession
options.c: Wordless groans reach the heart of God

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:26, with what does the Spirit intercede when expressed words fail?
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-05.learningObjective: Remember the manner of the Spirit's intercession.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: Beyond words, his intercession remains perfect.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of volume, but of depth.
feedbackWrong.c: A well-built speech is precisely what we lack.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-05.hint: It is too deep to become words.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-06.question: What links Romans 8:27 to Romans 8:34?
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-06.learningObjective: Link the two intercessions of Romans 8.
oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: Spirit in us and Christ at God's right hand: double intercession.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts affirm intercession on our behalf.
feedbackWrong.b: All intercession here is according to God's will.

oracao-pro-or-03-espirito-06.hint: See who else intercedes in the same chapter.

options.a: No one intercedes for the saints
options.b: Intercession against God's will
options.c: Christ also intercedes for us

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.question: In this challenge, Jesus teaches us to begin prayer with our urgent needs, before speaking of the Father.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Review the opening of the Lord's Prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The prayer begins with the Father and his name, not with urgencies.

feedbackWrong.true: Hallowed name and kingdom come before our petitions.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.hint: Remember the first line of the prayer taught.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Matthew 6:9, tap to whom Jesus tells us to direct the prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review the addressee of Jesus' prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: All prayer life begins by calling God this way.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the first petition, after calling him.
feedbackWrong.b: That is where he is, not whom we speak to.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.hint: It is the word that opens the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.question: According to Luke 18:1, why did Jesus tell the parable of the judge and the widow?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Review the purpose of the widow parable.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: The aim is stated before the story begins.

feedbackWrong.b: The widow speaks and insists: she is the example to follow.
feedbackWrong.c: The parable opens persistence; it does not close it.
feedbackWrong.d: The judge is a character in the lesson, not a practical warning.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.hint: The goal is in the first verse.

options.a: To teach to pray always and never lose heart
options.b: To show that widows should stay silent
options.c: To close the subject of prayer once and for all

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.question: Build Matthew 6:9 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the order of the Lord's Prayer opening.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Father, heaven, and hallowed name: the opening stays the same.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the call to our Father.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Follow the prayer word by word.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Matthew 6:10, we ask that God's rule called what would come?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the priority of the kingdom in prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: Before daily bread, his rule is asked for.

feedbackWrong.a: That is asked in the next verse, after it.
feedbackWrong.c: From evil we ask deliverance, at the end of the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is what should come to the earth.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.question: What does Luke 18:3 communicate that connects to this context?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Review persistence within a life of prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: She is the persistence piece in this life of prayer.

feedbackWrong.b: She returned to the judge again, without quitting.
feedbackWrong.c: Her lesson is precisely to keep coming back.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.hint: See the widow's role among the three teachings.

options.a: Insistence that never loses heart
options.b: Giving up at the first refusal
options.c: Prayer made only once

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Luke 18:3, tap who went to ask the city judge for justice.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: Without a defender, she herself goes, returns, and insists.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the setting of the story, not the person.
feedbackWrong.c: He is the other side of the case she brings.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.hint: Find the woman from the same city.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-08.question: Build Romans 8:26 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Help, our not knowing, and his intercession.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the help in our weaknesses.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.question: In Luke 18:7, the parable treats God as a just Father who defends his own, not as a reluctant judge.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Review the contrast between judge and God.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The unjust judge is the contrast that makes God shine.

feedbackWrong.false: Jesus' question expects trust in God's justice.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.hint: Separate the contrast character from God.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Matthew 6:10, tap the little word that equates earth and heaven in God's will.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Heaven is the measure of what is asked for the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the rule asked for, not the comparing word.
feedbackWrong.b: That is the needy place, not the comparison.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.hint: Find the short word between the two places.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.question: How do the Lord's Prayer and the widow parable complete each other on this trail?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus' form and perseverance walk together in a life of prayer.

feedbackWrong.a: One gives the form; the other, constancy in it.
feedbackWrong.b: The teachings are for disciples in general, without restriction.
feedbackWrong.c: The whole trail joins them on one path.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.hint: Think of form and constancy together.

options.a: Both dismiss any form of prayer
options.b: One is for leaders, the other only for widows
options.c: Both treat subjects with no connection
options.d: One teaches how to pray, the other teaches to keep going

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.question: How do the opening petitions of the Lord's Prayer connect?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the order of the first half of the prayer.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Name, kingdom, and will: the first half is all his.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the holiness of the Father's name.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Our needs have not even appeared yet.

options.a: The holiness of the name comes first
options.b: God's kingdom is asked for right after
options.c: His will is done on earth as in heaven

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Luke 18:1, to pray always is the opposite of losing heart called what?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the aim of the persistence parable.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: The widow's perseverance is the practice of that never.

feedbackWrong.b: Resting in God is good; the forbidden thing is another.
feedbackWrong.c: Silence can be prayer; the opposite here is a lost heart.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is losing heart in the middle of the way.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.question: What links Matthew 6:9 to Romans 8:15?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Relate Lord's Prayer and adoption in the Spirit.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: The Spirit of adoption makes the cry Jesus taught.

feedbackWrong.b: It is our Father: prayer of children and of family.
feedbackWrong.c: Romans trades slavery and fear for adoption.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.hint: See the cry of those who were adopted.

options.a: Children who cry Father
options.b: Prayer without God's family
options.c: Servile fear before God

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Romans 8:26, tap what we confess we do not know how to do as we ought.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: A life of prayer includes admitting that lack of knowing.

feedbackWrong.b: That is how he intercedes, not our task.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the ground of the help, not the act confessed.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.question: How does the widow's story advance in Luke 18:4–5?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Review the turn in the widow parable.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Refusal, insistent return, and the judge's decision.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the judge's initial refusal.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.hint: His decision is the last part.

options.a: The judge refuses to answer at first
options.b: The widow keeps coming to him without stopping
options.c: He decides to judge her case at last

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.question: On this trail, to pray well is always to speak perfectly, never lose heart inside, and never need the Spirit.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Interpret a life of prayer without perfectionism.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The trail assumes weakness and promises help, not perfection.

feedbackWrong.true: Not knowing how to pray is where the Spirit helps us.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Luke 18:7, tap for whom God promises to do justice when they cry to him.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review the promise of justice for the chosen.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Persistence rests on who God is for his own.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the constancy of the cry, not who receives it.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what God does, not for whom he does it.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.hint: Find the group after justice for.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.question: What reading sums up the life of prayer taught on this whole trail?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Choose the summary the trail supports.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Form of children, constancy of faith, and help in weakness.

feedbackWrong.a: The three texts speak of relationship, not technique.
feedbackWrong.b: It is our Father, in the plural, with a taught form.
feedbackWrong.d: The widow is praised precisely for not quitting.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.hint: Join the three teachings of the trail.

options.a: Master techniques until God is forced to answer
options.b: Each one prays alone, with no form or community at all
options.c: Pray as children, persist in faith, and depend on the Spirit
options.d: Giving up early proves true spiritual maturity

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.question: Which sequence reveals the theology of prayer on this trail?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: See the three teachings as one path.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Children who cry out and are helped by the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the Father whom the children call.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Intercession in weakness closes the path.

options.a: Children call God Father in prayer
options.b: They cry day and night asking for justice
options.c: The Spirit intercedes in their weakness

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Romans 8:26, the Spirit intercedes for us with what goes beyond words?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the manner of the Spirit's intercession.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: When the word ends, the intercession continues in him.

feedbackWrong.b: Volume is not the measure of that deep intercession.
feedbackWrong.c: No composition of ours is required in this text.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is inexpressible, greater than words.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.question: What links Luke 18:1 to Ephesians 6:18?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Link persistence and prayer in the Spirit.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: Always, at all times, and in the Spirit: the same perseverance.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts say to keep going, not to stop.
feedbackWrong.c: Christian perseverance is precisely in the Spirit.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.hint: Compare the always of the two texts.

options.a: Pray only once
options.b: Pray in the Spirit at all times
options.c: Persistence without the Holy Spirit

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Matthew 6:13, tap from what we ask not to fall, at the end of the prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.learningObjective: Review the petition for guard in the Lord's Prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: A life of prayer also asks for guard in the hour of testing.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the final declaration of trust, not the danger.
feedbackWrong.b: From evil we ask deliverance, one step later.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.hint: Find the test that can bring us down.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.question: Which sequence reveals the full logic of a life of prayer?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Understand the full logic of a life of prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom first, constancy in waiting, and his will at the end.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin where Jesus begins: with the Father.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.hint: God's will is the final measure.

options.a: Begin with the Father and his kingdom
options.b: Persist without losing heart while waiting
options.c: Depend on him according to God's will
